messages.content: my brother says he can help with my letter. does that mean he has already written it for me?
no. can help says that help is possible. it does not say that he has done the work or that he will write the whole letter.
what can i ask to make a plan?
you could ask: when would you have time to look at my letter with me?
i want to write it myself and only ask about the first sentence.
then say: could you look at my first sentence? i want to write the rest myself, but i am not sure how to begin.
he says he can look tomorrow. i need to send it today.
tell him that you need it today. he may not have time before then, so ask whether he can help before you need to send it.
write just my reply to him.
i need to send the letter today. do you have time to look at one sentence before then?
does that ask him to write the letter?
no. it asks him to look at one sentence. the rest is still your work.
what does i will walk to the library unless there is rain mean?
the walk is your plan, but rain could change it. if there is rain, the sentence leaves open what you will do instead.
use unless there is rain in the explanation.
unless there is rain says that rain is the thing that may change your plan to walk.
say it simply.
you plan to walk. if there is rain, you may do something else.
does that tell us whether there will be rain?
no. it says how rain could change your plan, rather than telling us what the weather will be.
add a choice for when there is rain.
i will walk to the library unless there is rain. if there is, i will stay home and read.
now make it about tomorrow and not today.
tomorrow, i will walk to the library unless there is rain. if there is, i will stay home and read.
two people use the same phone. if one reads a message, does that mean both have read it?
no. using the same phone does not mean both people see every message. you need more information about who read that one.
one person read it and told the other what it said.
then both may know the information, but only one was said to have read the message. hearing about it is different from reading it yourself.
can you make a short story with that difference?

a mother reads a message on the family phone. it says that her sister will visit after lunch. she talks to her son, who is drawing at the table. later, he says he knows his aunt is coming. when asked whether he read the message, he says no. his mother told him.
is the son wrong to say he knows about the visit?
no. someone can learn information from another person. he does not have to read the original message to know what his mother told him.
does this say the aunt has already come?
no. the aunt will visit after lunch. the story does not say that she is already there.
say that part simply.
the aunt will visit after lunch. the story does not say that she is already there.
my child drew a circle and wants me to help turn it into a story. keep the story about the circle, not a whole new picture.

a small circle sits alone in the middle of a page. it asks why there is nothing around it. the child draws another circle near it, then a line between them. now the first circle has someone to talk to and a road for visiting. they spend the afternoon choosing where the road could go next.
can a real circle talk?
no. the two things in the picture talk only in the made up story. the child can write their words or say the words for them.
make that simple.
no. they talk only in the story. the child can say the words for them.
let the road stay short because they want to be near each other.
they choose to keep the road short. they like being close enough to talk without a long journey. the child leaves the rest of the page empty for another story later.
did you add a square or a house?
no. the story only added another circle and a line to the first circle.
we have four garments on a table. two are mine, one is my sister garment, and one is my brother garment. i want to put them in groups by person.
you can make a group of two for yourself, one for your sister, and one for your brother. keep a group for each person rather than using color as the rule.
fix my grammar with words from our list.
you can say: two garments are mine, one is for my sister, and one is for my brother. then keep a group for each person.
for does not always mean it is theirs already. i want the sentence to say whose it is.
two garments are mine, one is hers, and one is his. if you have already said who she and he are, that keeps the meaning clear.
what if both mine are blue and the other two are blue too?
then color will not help you make groups by person. you need to know whose each garment is, rather than only its color.
are there still four garments after making the groups?
yes. putting them in groups changes their order or place, rather than adding or taking away garments.
write a story where a teacher writes a question on a page and waits before answering it.

a teacher writes: how do we know? on a large page. a child says that a story person must be happy because she has a new book. the teacher asks what the story says about her feelings. they read the page and find that the person wanted a different book. the child sees that getting a book did not tell the whole story. the teacher leaves the question on the wall so they can use it again.
can you say story person another way?
a person in the story.
what did the child know at first?
the child knew that the person had a new book. the child had not yet used the detail that the person wanted a different book.
say that last part simply.
the child had not yet used the detail that the person wanted a different book.
what question could the teacher ask after they read that detail?
can someone get a book and still wish it were a different one?
does the new detail tell us that the person does not like any books?
no. it is about one book and one wish. it does not tell us how the person feels about every book.
i always make tea before writing a letter. today i started the letter first and remembered the tea later.
you changed the order for one day. did the letter feel different, or did you only remember the tea later?
i just forgot about the tea until i finished the first sentence.
then the first sentence got your time before the tea did. you can still make tea now if you want it.
can you write this as a little story, without saying i could not write without tea?
i usually make tea before writing a letter. today, i sat down and wrote the first sentence, then remembered the tea.
does that mean i made tea? i only told you i remembered it.
no. the story keeps that part open. it says that you remembered the tea, but not what you did after that.
write only the facts.
i usually make tea before writing a letter. today, i wrote the first sentence, then remembered the tea.
keep just the sentence about today.
today, i wrote the first sentence, then remembered the tea.
my friend sent the same request in two messages. does that mean they want two books instead of one?
not by itself. your friend may have sent it again to make sure you saw it, rather than to ask for another object. look at the words or ask if the number is not clear.
use simple words.
the same request in two messages does not always mean two books. your friend may just want to know that you saw the first message.
write a kind question asking how many books they want.
do you want one book, or are you asking for two?
make the question more kind.
just to check, do you want one book or two?
they say one. now i find two different books they might mean. what can i ask?
which book would you like me to bring?
does the answer one tell me which book?
no. one gives the number. you still need to know which book is wanted.
wanted is in the list. can you make the last answer shorter?
no. one says how many, rather than which one.
two people ride the same train. does that mean they will get off at the same station?
no. each can get off at a different station. being on the same train does not give the same end place for every person.
say it simply.
no. each can get off at a different station.
keep just the answer no.
no.
write a short story with a brother and sister who start together but go to different places.

a brother and sister get on a train together. she is going to town to meet a friend, while he is visiting their uncle in another place. they talk until her station. she gets off, and he is still on the train. they plan to talk about the day when they get home.
make the last part simple.
she gets off, and he is still on the train. they plan to talk about the day when they get home.
does the story say who gets home first?
no. it gives the order for leaving the train, but not the order for coming home.
my uncle asked me to bring the blue book. there are three blue books on the shelf. i do not know which one he wants.
you can ask for another detail, such as the name of the book or what it is about. color alone is not enough to choose between three blue books.
he says the one about a garden. i see only one with a garden picture. can i be sure from that?
not always. a picture of a garden might be on a book about something else. if you can, look at the name and a little of the writing to check what the book is about.
write a short question asking for its name.
what is the name of the blue book you want me to bring?
he does not remember. can i bring him all three?
you can ask whether that would help, if you have room to carry them. that may let him look and choose, rather than having you choose without enough information.
write that request.
would you like me to bring all three blue books so you can choose the right one?
does asking that mean i must carry them before he answers?
no. you are asking whether it would help. the request does not say that you have already brought them.
i want the room ready before my friend comes. i only need to clear the table and put out two chairs. help me make a short plan.
first, take the things off the table and put them in the right place. then bring two chairs to the table. check that there is room for both people to sit.
clear is in my first sentence but not the list. say my request simply.
help me make room on the table and put two chairs near it before my friend comes.
i have done the chairs first. is the plan wrong now?
no. the order can change if the work still gets done. you can put the things away from the table next.
i mean i want to know if i should change the plan.
no. the chairs are ready, and the table still needs work. finish that part next.
what if my friend comes before the table is ready?
you can tell them what is left and ask whether they would like to sit on the sofa for a moment. you do not need to say the room is ready when it is not.
ask them to sit on the sofa.
could you sit on the sofa for a moment while i finish the table?
i need a reply from a father to a child who says they found a key.
is this a made up conversation for a story, or a real message you want to write?
it is for a story. the father should not know what the key opens.
then he could say: where did you find it? let us look at it together before choosing a door to try.
can he say that it is the garden key if i did not give that detail?
not while keeping your request that he does not know. he could ask whether anyone has seen it before, but saying what it opens would give him an answer he does not have in your story.
write a short conversation where he asks the mother too.
where did you find the key? under the table. i do not know which door it is for. shall we ask your mother? yes. she might have seen it before.
tell me what i asked for simply.
you asked for a short conversation where the father and child ask the mother about the key.
did that last conversation say the mother knows the answer?
no. it says she might have seen it. the story still needs her reply to tell us what she knows.
